Tu auras naturellement envie de revenir terminer ce que tu as commencé. ✨ Romantise tes révisions Crée un environnement que tu apprécies : une playlist, une boisson, une jolie lumière ou un bureau rangé. Let’s be honest, romantic desks, pastel highlighters, and 5AM miracle routines aren’t fixing your grades. Here’s what actually works (and nobody posts because it’s not aesthetic): 1️⃣ Study in ugly places Your brain forms stronger memory cues when it’s not fully relaxed. When you study on your bed or in a cozy setup, your brain associates the space with rest → not recall. A slightly uncomfortable chair, library desk, or quiet corner keeps your brain alert, which improves focus and retention. Aesthetic ≠ effective. 2️⃣ Start with the hardest topic first Most students waste peak brain energy on easy chapters “to build confidence.” That’s a trap. Your focus is highest at the beginning of a study session, use it for the topic you avoid the most. By the time your energy dips, even small wins feel doable. Hard-first = faster syllabus completion. 3️⃣ Write bad notes on purpose Rewriting textbooks neatly is passive studying. Messy notes mean your brain is processing, not copying. When you struggle to frame points in your own words, your brain builds neural connections. If your notes look ugly but make sense to you, they’re gold. 4️⃣ Teach a wall (or yourself) out loud Silent reading gives false confidence. Explaining out loud forces your brain to retrieve information without help. If you freeze or overcomplicate, that’s the exact gap you need to fix. Teaching exposes weak spots faster than rereading ever will. 5️⃣ Stop studying when you’re still focused This sounds wrong but it’s powerful. This pre exam routine saved me grades and GPA. This routine works because it forces your brain to actually retrieve and apply information instead of just recognizing it. Blurting and active recall strengthen memory by making you pull knowledge out under pressure (just like an exam), while condensing everything into one page builds connections so you understand the big picture instead of memorizing random facts. Creating mock exams and targeting what you missed turns your weaknesses into strengths fast, which is where most people plateau because they just reread notes. It’s basically like training in the gym,you don’t grow by watching workouts, you grow by stressing the muscle, this method stresses your brain in the exact way exams do, so when test day comes, it feels familiar instead of overwhelming. Dental experiences in childhood don’t just stay in childhood — they shape how someone feels about dentistry for life. We see it every day: adults who avoid the dentist because of fear that started when they were little. Being restrained, rushed, or treated without emotional support can create real dental trauma that carries into adulthood as anxiety, avoidance, and even panic. At Smiley Kids Dental, we believe no child should be forced through treatment. That’s why we never recommend papoosing (physical restraint) as a form of care. Instead, we focus on: ✨ Gentle, age-appropriate communication ✨ Trust-building and tell-show-do techniques ✨ A calm, kid-centered environment ✨ And when needed, safe sedation options to keep children comfortable and stress-free Our goal isn’t just to fix teeth — it’s to protect a child’s emotional well-being and help them grow into adults who aren’t afraid of the dentist. I run a tutoring business — this is the 3-step system we use to prepare students for any exam (and actually improve grades): 1. Master the spec (this is your map) Most students revise everything instead of what actually gets marks. Go through the spec line by line and ask: could I explain this simply? If not, that’s your gap. This stops wasted time and keeps revision focused. 2. Active recall + past papers Reading notes isn’t revision. Blurting, flashcards, teaching it out loud, and lots of past paper questions is what builds memory + exam technique. Do questions early — not just at the end. 3. Fix mistakes properly  Don’t just mark and move on. Write out corrections, understand why you got it wrong, and track patterns (e.g. “I always drop marks on 6 markers” or “I rush calculations”). Then target those specifically. The main thing is making sure you look after yourself though!!  #gcse #alevels #tutoring #businessowner #productivity
